transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-22 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Jonah (Redwood Solutions), Jared (Quantaco Head of ML), Priya (Infra), Marcus (Product), Anita (SRE)

Auto-summary: Quick run through of latest benchmarks; primary focus on tokens/sec per dollar, how caching and batching impact effective unit cost, and next steps to finalize pilot pricing.

00:00 Samir: hey everyone, um this is our weekly poc sync to go over the cost econ numbers we ran last week, we'll review the spreadsheet and then talk tradeoffs.
00:12 Jared: hey Samir, hi Elena, yep excited to see results - we've had the team run the small end-to-end with our prompt set.
00:18 Elena: quick note, on the runs we used the rdx-7b-q8 model variant for the initial cost table, run on dedicated A100-ish nodes, we tried batch sizes of 1, 8 and 16.
00:29 Priya: right the infra team saw some weird tail latency at batch 16 under peak concurrency, I think kernel warmup?
00:36 Jonah: mhm, we expected some warmup behavior. The raw tokens/sec numbers look like: batch1 ~ 120 tokens/sec per GPU, batch8 ~ 560, batch16 ~ 900 but latency p95 jumped to ~600ms from ~220ms.
00:50 Marcus: so cost per 1k tokens at batch 16 was how much again?
00:56 Elena: in the sheet we show approx $0.012 per 1k tokens at batch1, $0.0042 at batch8 and $0.0027 at batch16 when you amortize GPU-hour. But caveat, these assume sustained throughput and no caching.
01:11 Jared: ok that delta looks big, but user-facing latency matters to our product flows - product team is still aiming for 300ms median and sub-600ms p95 on chat replies.
01:21 Samir: right and that's the tradeoff. We also tested prefix caching - so for our conversational flows we had a cache hit rate of 48% in this run, when prefix cache hits occur effective tokens/sec/$ improves dramatically.
01:33 Anita: just to clarify, prefix caching means we avoid re-computing initial context KV for repeated prompts right?
01:39 Elena: yes, prefix/KV cache avoids the first N tokens compute; in our experiment with a 48% hit, effective cost per 1k tokens dropped ~35% compared to no cache because you save the initial decode cost. Note - cache eviction patterns matter, and your prompt diversity will change hit rate.
01:55 Priya: our preliminary sim shows cache hit could be as low as 20% in a full prod distribution because product mixes variants, so we shouldn't bake in the 48% as baseline.
02:05 Samir: agree - that's why we recommend modeling a conservative and optimistic scenario in the spreadsheet. We put conservative at 25% hit and optimistic at 60% hit.
02:14 Jared: can you talk about the tokens/sec per dollar metric specifically? I want to show that to execs - what's the definition you're using?
02:20 Elena: tokens/sec/$ is basically throughput per GPU-dollar where tokens/sec measured sustained at steady state and $ is GPU cost per unit time. For our sheet we normalized to tokens per second per dollar per GPU-hour. So higher is better.
02:34 Marcus: one question - are we including system overhead (I/O, pre/post processing) in those numbers?
02:40 Elena: good call - the base numbers are model-only inference time on the GPU plus a small fixed overhead per request for pre/post. We have separate lines in the sheet where we add 15% overhead for your stack, but we can change that if you have better estimates.
02:53 Jared: we do have extra reranking steps occasionally, so we should add a rerank multiplier for 10-20% additional cost, yes please.
03:03 Samir: noted, we'll add a rerank multiplier. On batching tradeoffs: batch larger to get lower cost but you increase tail latency and risk of head-of-line blocking in chat.
03:14 Priya: what about smart batching? i.e., dynamic batch assembly so high-priority requests bypass large batches?
03:20 Elena: we support dynamic batching policies: latency SLO based routing to smaller pools, and you can configure a small fraction of capacity as low-latency reserved to keep p95 lower. That will increase unit cost a little but protects SLAs.
03:31 Jared: can we quantify that? like cost delta for reserving 10% capacity to low-latency pool?
03:36 Elena: in a rough calc, reserving 10% low-latency increases per-token cost about 8-12% for the overall traffic mix because you're carrying some unfilled GPU cycles. We'll put exact numbers in the sheet.
03:48 Marcus: how does quantization affect the numbers? we heard q4/q8 has different perf curves.
03:54 Elena: q8 gives you a good win on memory and sometimes throughput; quantization sometimes increases throughput for small models by 10-30% depending on kernel; for rdx-7b-q8 we saw about 25% cost improvement vs float16 baseline at similar latency. But quality testing needed.
04:10 Jared: quality is non-negotiable - we need to run our eval prompts to ensure no regression.
04:14 Samir: agreed - part of the plan: Elena will run the quantized model on your prompt set and produce a quality diff table.
04:21 Priya: about caching savings - can we simulate different hit rates quickly?
04:25 Elena: yes we can run the bench harness that replays your prompt set with variable session reuse and produce cache hit rates and effective cost. We'll run 25%, 50%, 75% scenarios.
04:35 Jared: perfect. Also on fallback policies - if dedicated capacity is constrained, we want to route to hosted with a slightly cheaper model and acceptable latency. How do you recommend modeling that for cost?
04:46 Samir: we typically add a fallback multiplier and a quality delta line. If you route 20% of traffic to a lower-cost hosted variant, cost reduces but quality/latency changes - we can model multiple routing policies in the same spreadsheet.
04:59 Marcus: any notes on KV cache eviction and memory sizing? Priya had concerns about memory pressure on smaller nodes.
05:06 Elena: yes, KV sizing depends on longest context retained and number of concurrent sessions. For your 8k context target we recommend nodes with 80GB GPU memory or shard across two GPUs. We'll include recommended configs.
05:20 Priya: ok that helps. For the bench runs you mentioned earlier, will you provide the raw traces and token timelines?
05:27 Elena: yes, we'll upload raw traces, per-token timings, and latency distributions to the shared folder.
05:33 Samir: to recap next steps: Samir to update cost sheet with rerank multipliers and routing scenarios; Elena to run batching + quantization + caching scenarions and upload traces; Jared to share the 1k prompt set. We'll meet next week.
05:48 Jared: sounds good. Quick nit - some of the transcription here could be off, there was cross-talk when we talked about q8.
05:55 Samir: noted. Any final questions?
06:00 Marcus: none from me. Thanks.
06:03 Priya: we'll aim to get infra confirmations by 7/28 as discussed.
06:07 Samir: great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the sheet and runbook.

End of transcript.

Referenced artifacts: cost_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx (shared link in chat), benchmark_traces/batch16_run1.tar.gz (link), private-deployment-runbook.md (link).

Quality notes: transcription occasionally mislabels names and substitutes model names (rdx-7b-q8 was a shorthand), timestamps approx every 15-90s depending on speaker turns.
